regulation: EPA Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure rule
requirement_summary: Each oil production container installation must use at least one listed method to avoid discharges; the option used at about 250 batteries is high level sensors that generate and transmit an alarm signal to the computer where the facility has a computer production control system
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 250 of 410 central tank batteries rely on this option
crosswalk_source: Author mapping
current_state: High-level alarms reach SYS-P1; wells stop on loss of tank level signal
evidence: SPCC plans; alarm list; controller settings
gap_description: No written procedure for when the alarm path fails (SCADA, network, or cyber outage): who shuts in or gauges, and how fast
remediation_action: Alarm-loss procedure with a 4-hour decision to shut in or gauge; test at 10 batteries a year (P01 PD-004)

regulation: EPA discharge notice (Clean Water Act section 311)
requirement_summary: The person in charge of an onshore facility must immediately notify the National Response Center of a discharge of oil in a quantity that may be harmful (violates water quality standards, or causes a sheen, discoloration, sludge, or emulsion)
crosswalk_source: Author mapping
current_state: HSE spill procedure with the National Response Center number; on-call HSE coordinator
gap_description: Procedure assumes control room phones and email; no offline path if the IOC is isolated during a cyber incident
remediation_action: Offline contact cards and satellite phones at the IOC, BCC, and field offices
